annotation_description: Suspicious Bookcase is a passive 0/4 defender that doesn't advance the game plan. Hangarback Walker for X=1 is a growing threat that synergizes with multiple cards in hand (Ugin's Mastery triggers on colorless creature cast for manifest, Ruins of Oran-Rief can add a counter when played later, Abstruse Archaic can copy its death trigger). In a 4-player game, the 0/4 wall provides minimal defensive value.

message: Choose spell or ability to play: Myriad Landscape
chosen_display: 2. {2}, {T}, Sacrifice Myriad Landscape: Search your library for up to two basic land cards that share a land type, put them onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle.
annotation_description: MiMo Stoic activated Myriad Landscape's sacrifice ability while Solemn Simulacrum is on the stack (being cast). The Myriad Landscape costs {2} + tap + sacrifice, which uses the 2 colorless mana from the Mountain and Plains (the only untapped lands), plus taps and sacrifices the Landscape itself. This means after Solemn Simulacrum resolves and fetches a land, MiMo will have lands but they'll all enter tapped. The issue is that Mind Stone is in hand and costs {2}. If MiMo had played the Study Hall from hand first (land drop), then tapped Mountain + Plains for {2} to cast Mind Stone, they would have had Mind Stone on the battlefield as a mana rock, while keeping Myriad Landscape for a future turn when they could better afford to sacrifice it (or sacrifice it next turn with more mana available). Sacrificing Myriad Landscape on turn 4 with Solemn Simulacrum already fetching a land means heavy investment in ramp this turn while deploying no artifacts for Osgir synergy. However, getting two basics is strong ramp, so this is debatable — but the sequencing of not playing Mind Stone first (using the 2 available mana) before committing to the Landscape activation seems suboptimal since Mind Stone could have been cast with the Mountain + Plains mana, and the Landscape sacrificed on a later turn.

Fetched 2 Plains with Myriad Landscape when hand contains Thopter Engineer (2R), Hellkite Tyrant (4RR), and already has a Plains in hand. With only 1 Mountain on board, red mana is the bottleneck. Getting 2 Mountains would provide 3R+1W from lands, with the Plains in hand covering future white needs.

message: Choose spell or ability to play: Mind Stone
chosen_display: 2. {1}, {T}, Sacrifice Mind Stone: Draw a card.
annotation_description: MiMo Stoic sacrificed Mind Stone to draw a card on turn 4, but they have 6 cards in hand including Hellkite Tyrant (6 mana), Thopter Engineer (3 mana), and Key to the City (2 mana). With only 5 lands and Mind Stone, they had 6 mana sources. Sacrificing Mind Stone drops them to 5 mana sources, making it harder to cast Hellkite Tyrant on turn 5 (needs 6 mana including RR). They also have a land in hand (Plains or Mountain) they could play, but even with that they'd only have 6 lands next turn - exactly enough for Hellkite Tyrant if they kept Mind Stone. By sacrificing it, they now need to draw into another land or delay their biggest threat. The Mind Stone was more valuable as ramp toward the 6-mana Hellkite Tyrant than as a card draw at this stage.

message: Choose spell or ability to play: Counterflux
chosen_display: 1. Cast Counterflux: Counter target spell you don't control.
annotation_description: Karmic Guide was cast by Qwen3 ESPN who has an empty graveyard, meaning its powerful ETB reanimation ability would have no valid target. Additionally, Karmic Guide has echo {3}{W}{W} which Qwen3 would struggle to pay, likely sacrificing it next upkeep. Counterflux is a premium uncounterable counter spell that was wasted on an essentially blank 2/2 flyer.

message: Select a player, planeswalker, or battle to attack
annotation_description: During another player's combat step (Grk41F Vet's), Grk41F Vet declined to activate Mazemind Tome. With 8 lands/artifacts on the battlefield and mana available, they could have used Mazemind Tome to scry 1 (costs just {T} and a page counter) at no real cost. This is a pure-upside ability that improves card quality. The Suspicious Bookcase activation would cost {3} and a tap, which is more debatable, but the Mazemind Tome scry is essentially free card selection that was left on the table.

Grk41F Vet declined to use Mazemind Tome's activated ability during combat (likely at end of an opponent's turn or during their own combat step with open mana). With 4 untapped Wastes and Mazemind Tome available, they could have used the scry ability ({T}, put a page counter: Scry 1) for free, or paid {2} plus {T} to draw a card. Instead they passed and then played Blast Zone from hand. Since Mazemind Tome tapping doesn't cost any mana for the scry mode, declining a free scry is leaving value on the table. Even if they wanted to use it on a later turn, there's no downside to scrying now since it's a 'may' effect on what you do with the card.

Passed with 5 colorless mana available when they could have cast Ugin's Mastery (cost {4}), which has excellent synergy with their hand full of colorless creatures (Steel Hellkite, Abstruse Archaic, Ancient Stone Idol). At minimum, they should have activated Mazemind Tome to scry or draw a card, which is pure upside with unused mana.

Grk41F Vet declined to use Mazemind Tome during the combat step. With 8 lands/artifacts on the battlefield and mana available (3 untapped Wastes + Forge of Heroes + Ruins of Oran-Rief provide mana), they could have at minimum used Mazemind Tome's scry ability (tap + put a page counter) for free card selection, or paid 2 + tap to draw a card. Since it's their own combat step and the Tome would be tapped afterward anyway (they're not attacking with it), there's no downside to using it here. With a hand full of expensive colorless creatures (Steel Hellkite at 6, Ancient Stone Idol at 10, Abstruse Archaic at 4, Ugin's Mastery at 4), card selection or draw would help find lands or cheaper plays. This is a missed pure-upside activation opportunity.

Grk41F Vet has 6 mana available (3 Wastes untapped + Forge of Heroes + Ruins of Oran-Rief + Mazemind Tome's tap). With Mazemind Tome having page counters accumulating, using it for scry or draw at end of turn is free value. The player declined to activate any abilities during post-combat main, leaving mana unused. Mazemind Tome's draw ability costs {2} + tap + page counter, which was affordable, and the scry ability is even cheaper at just tap + page counter. Not using available mana on a card-advantage artifact when there's nothing better to spend mana on is leaving value on the table.

MiMo Stoic cast Ichor Wellspring before playing a land from hand. They have Plains and Mountain in hand and haven't made their land drop yet. By playing a land first (getting to 7 mana sources), they could have cast both Ichor Wellspring (2 mana) and Thopter Engineer (3 mana) in the same turn, developing the board more efficiently.

message: Select a player, planeswalker, or battle to attack
annotation_description: Grk41F Vet declined to use Mazemind Tome during combat, when they had untapped mana and the Tome available. With 3 Wastes untapped (plus Forge of Heroes and Ruins of Oran-Rief), they could have used Mazemind Tome to either scry 1 for free (just tap) or pay 2 and tap to draw a card. Since this is during their own combat step and they have no attackers creating pressure, there's no reason not to at least scry 1 with Mazemind Tome, as it's a pure-upside activated ability that helps improve future draws at no cost beyond tapping the artifact.

Grk41F Vet has Mazemind Tome untapped with available mana (Ruins of Oran-Rief and Forge of Heroes are untapped, providing 2 colorless mana). They could have activated Mazemind Tome to either scry 1 (tap + put a page counter, costs 0 mana) or pay 2 to draw a card (2 mana + tap + page counter). With all their Wastes tapped but two colorless-producing lands untapped, they had exactly 2 mana available. Using Mazemind Tome to draw a card (paying {2}, {T}, put a page counter) would have been pure upside - they're not using those lands for anything else this turn since it's their precombat main phase and they can't cast anything meaningful with just 2 colorless mana. At minimum, they should have used the free scry 1 activation to improve card quality.

Declined to activate Mazemind Tome's scry ability before Mystic Forge resolves. Scrying 1 at this point costs no mana (just tapping Tome) and would help set up the top card of the library to maximize Mystic Forge's value immediately upon resolution.

Chose to scry 1 with Mazemind Tome instead of drawing a card, despite having exactly 2 mana available from untapped Ruins of Oran-Rief and Forge of Heroes to pay for the draw ability. Drawing a card provides strictly more value than scrying 1, and the 2 mana would otherwise go unused. While scry has some synergy with the incoming Mystic Forge, drawing a concrete card is better than merely rearranging the top of the library.

Grk41F Vet declined to use Mazemind Tome during the combat step (likely end of opponent's turn or their own combat). With 2 page counters already on Mazemind Tome, they could have used it to scry 1 (for {T}) or pay {2},{T} to draw a card and put a 3rd page counter on it. All their lands are tapped, so they can't pay {2} for the draw mode, but they could still tap Mazemind Tome to scry 1 for free (just {T} and adding a page counter). Scrying for free is pure upside that helps find key cards like lands or threats. Declining a free scry is a small but clear mistake.

MiMo Stoic cast Sol Ring into open blue mana from Gem25F Johnny, who had 8 mana available (including Izzet Signet and multiple Islands) and was holding Aethersnatch. Sol Ring is a powerful mana rock, but casting it when an opponent has 6+ blue mana open and could steal it is risky. More importantly, Gem25F Johnny successfully cast Aethersnatch to steal the Sol Ring, meaning MiMo Stoic lost a card and gave an opponent a Sol Ring. MiMo Stoic had other productive plays available - Thopter Engineer (3 mana, creates a token), Battlemage's Bracers (3 mana), or Rip Apart (2 mana to deal with a threat) - that would have been less painful if countered/stolen. Playing the Mountain first and then casting a different spell would have been better sequencing.

Used Aetherize, a premium mass-bounce spell, to bounce only 2 modest creatures (Abstruse Archaic 3/4 and Solemn Simulacrum 2/2) while at 40 life. Only preventing 5 damage at full life. Worse, bouncing Solemn Simulacrum gives Grk41F Vet another ETB land-fetch trigger when replayed.

message: Select card to discard (selected 0 of 2, min 2)
annotation_description: Discarded Worn Powerstone despite having zero mana rocks and a hand full of expensive 6+ mana cards (Steel Hellkite, Dreamstone Hedron, Soul of New Phyrexia). Worn Powerstone would provide critical acceleration. Solemn Simulacrum is also decent ramp/value that was discarded.

With Wastes in hand, playing the land first would give 6 mana, enabling Dreamstone Hedron - a critical ramp piece that taps for 3 colorless mana. Grk41F Vet has lost significant mana rocks (Worn Powerstone, etc.) and desperately needs ramp to cast their expensive hand (Steel Hellkite, Soul of New Phyrexia). Abstruse Archaic is a decent body but its copy ability has limited immediate value with no other colorless activated/triggered abilities to copy.

Grk41F Vet had a Wastes in hand but did not play it before casting their spell. Playing the land first would have been free value - an extra mana source costs nothing and should always be done before committing to spells.

Grk41F Vet activated Ruins of Oran-Rief's +1/+1 counter ability, but there are no creatures on their battlefield at all, let alone a colorless creature that entered this turn. There is no valid target for this ability. This wastes the tap of a land that could have produced {C} mana instead.

annotation_description: Grk41F Vet declined to activate Bonders' Enclave during combat to draw a card. Grk41F Vet declined to activate Bonders' Enclave to draw a card during combat, despite controlling creatures with power 4+ (It That Betrays 11/11, Ancient Stone Idol 12/12) and having sufficient untapped lands to pay {3},{T}.
